independent_computation.method: The leaf is a prose justification, so the check is a truth-check of each clause against the cached wiki text and cached atom classification for item 3157.

step_1_enumerate_declared_families.result: The new value's universal claim 'Every declared family on this item is a defence' is false by direct enumeration: (a) no 'defence' family exists in the cached taxonomy at all, and (b) two of the three distinct declared families are 'stats' and 'damage'. The 'damage' atom (damage.resistance-mitigation) is itself keyed to behavior 'Time Stop', i.e. the represented mechanic is classified into the damage family, not a durability-only one.

step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.wiki_text: stasis ... 'but also unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items'
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.atom_corroboration: data/atoms/items.json "3157" carries atom_id 'damage.basic_attack' with evidence 'active:Time Stop@kw:basic attack' and value 2.5 - the parser itself read the active as touching basic attacks for 2.5 s.
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.arithmetic: Under the engine's renewal counting N(T) = floor(AS * u * T) (docs/math-foundations.md 1.1), 2.5 s of stasis inside a fight window is 2.5 s of zero action: it removes floor-level auto swings and every cast start in that interval. For any AS*u > 0.4 the swing count strictly drops, and all ability cast starts in [t0, t0+2.5] are suppressed. Therefore the mechanic changes outgoing TDD (downward) whenever it is used inside the window - it is not durability-only.
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.result: The new value's second clause ('the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD') is contradicted by the item's own cached effect text.

step_3_check_the_old_value.claim_a: 'Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input' - consistent with the cache: the effect lives under active[] (not passives[]), riotDescription tags it <active>, and its duration is a fixed bounded 2.5 s ({{fd|2.5}}), so the only free parameter a scenario can supply is whether/how many active seconds fall inside the window.
step_3_check_the_old_value.claim_b: 'item presence alone never assumes stasis' - consistent with the cache and with the project's fail-closed convention: an activated item requires an explicit activation; nothing in data/items.json 3157 makes the stasis automatic (contrast a passive entry, of which this item has none).
step_3_check_the_old_value.result: Both clauses of the old value are true against the cached source, and the old wording is also the safe one: it preserves the fact that stasis seconds do affect TDD once declared, instead of asserting the effect can never touch TDD.

conclusion: The new value asserts two things the cached wiki text and cached atom classification both refute: Zhonya's Hourglass declares 'stats' and 'damage' families (not only a defence), and its Time Stop stasis explicitly suppresses basic attacks and ability casts for 2.5 s, which changes outgoing TDD. The old value states the correct, source-consistent rule. Verdict: old_value_correct.
notes: Caveat on identification: the item at item_coverage[1] was inferred from the old value's mention of 'Time Stop'. If the change also reordered item_coverage entries so index 1 now names a different item, this receipt judges the Zhonya's Hourglass reason only.

Aside: the cached atom classification for 3157 maps Time Stop to 'damage.resistance-mitigation' (data/item-atoms/3157.json) while data/atoms/items.json maps the same branch to 'damage.basic_attack'. Both agree it is damage-family, but the two atom stores disagree on the behavior label - worth a look independently of this leaf.
